bearing.guide.track_placement.text_1: Train tracks are a dedicated kind of rail, built for train contraptions
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_2: To lay a long row at once, first click the end of a track that is already there
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_3: ...then click a second spot, or another track, to fill the gap between them
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_4: Connections are not limited to straight lines: they can bend and climb as well
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_5: Without help, the connection makes both halves of a turn the same size
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_6: For a different shape, connect while the sprint key is down...
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_7: ...and the widest curve that fits between the two ends is used instead
bearing.guide.track_placement.text_8: Put paving blocks in your off-hand and a bed of them goes under the new track
bearing.guide.track_portal.text_1: Lay a track so that it runs straight into a nether portal...
bearing.guide.track_portal.text_2: ...and it will try to build a matching track at the portal on the other side
bearing.guide.track_portal.text_3: Trains running on it can now cross over into another dimension
bearing.guide.track_chunks.text_1: Tracks keep working even where no chunks are loaded
bearing.guide.track_chunks.text_2: Parts of the world nobody is near pose no obstacle to a running train
bearing.guide.track_chunks.text_3: Station stops and red signals are still respected out there
bearing.guide.track_chunks.text_4: Drills and other machines carried on board, however, stay idle there
bearing.guide.track_chunks.text_5: As soon as a player comes close, the train shows up again
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_1: A station is tied to the track you click with it before placing it close by
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_2: Stations act as the named stops of your whole railway network
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_3: Open its interface and switch to Assembly Mode to build a new train
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_4: While assembling, trains following a schedule will not come to this station
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_5: Using Train Casing on a track turns that spot into a bogey
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_6: Click the same spot again to switch between the available bogey styles
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_7: Use Super Glue to make the other blocks part of the train
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_8: Fuel found in chests or barrels on board makes the finished train go faster
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_9: Anything kept in an Item Vault is never burned as fuel, though
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_10: No train works without a set of Train Controls among its blocks
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_11: A second set facing the other way lets it leave stations in either direction
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_12: Back in the station interface, confirm the assembly to finish the train
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_13: Turning a train back into blocks is only possible at a station
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_14: Using a map on a station puts a named marker for it on the map
bearing.guide.train_assembly.text_15: With a Wrench, an assembled train can be moved onto tracks close by
bearing.guide.auto_schedule.text_1: A schedule tells the driver of a train where to go
bearing.guide.auto_schedule.text_2: A comparator reading the station outputs a signal while a train is there
bearing.guide.auto_schedule.text_3: Keep in mind that trains can only pull in from the direction the station points to
bearing.guide.auto_schedule.text_4: A station can also hand out new schedules to trains by itself
bearing.guide.auto_schedule.text_5: Any train stopping there gets a copy of the schedule placed on the station
bearing.guide.auto_schedule.text_6: Unlike handing it over by hand, the original item stays with the station
bearing.guide.train_signal_placement.tex: Click a train track, then put the signal down next to it
Signals direct the traffic of every train that is not steered by a player
Trains on a schedule never pass a signal from its back side
...that changes once a second signal facing the other way is added
Nixie tubes placed on a signal make its light easier to see
bearing.guide.train_signal_signaling.tex: Signals cut a track up into separate segments
While one train occupies a segment, no other train may enter it
This way, every segment only ever holds a single train
A Wrench switches a signal to its second mode
A segment starting at a brass signal usually ends at regular signals
This kind of signal can hold trains back for one more reason
It keeps out any train that, after entering...
...could not get out of the segment again right away
That way, waiting trains queue up outside a busy segment instead of blocking it
bearing.guide.train_signal_redstone.head: Overriding Signals with Redstone
bearing.guide.train_signal_redstone.text: Powering a signal with redstone forces it to show red
The other way round, a red signal gives out a comparator signal
bearing.guide.train_schedule.text_1: Schedules let trains be driven by someone other than you
bearing.guide.train_schedule.text_2: Its editor opens when you use the item with a right-click
bearing.guide.train_schedule.text_3: When it is set up, give the schedule to a train driver
bearing.guide.train_schedule.text_4: Drivers can be any mob, or a blaze burner, on the seat facing the Train Controls
bearing.guide.train_schedule.text_5: A lead makes it easier to bring a mob over to its seat
bearing.guide.train_schedule.text_6: You can take a schedule back from its driver whenever you like
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_1: Every train contraption must carry Train Controls
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_2: After assembly, right-click them to take the wheel
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_3: Use your movement keys to speed up, slow down and pick a direction at junctions
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_4: Scroll the mouse wheel to adjust the top speed if you like
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_5: Hold space to bring the train in to a station nearby
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_6: Turning the train back into blocks requires a station
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_7: Press the sprint key to sound any whistles built into the train
bearing.guide.train_controls.text_8: Sneak, or click the controls once more, to let go of the train
bearing.guide.track_observer.text_1: Like a station, the observer links to a track you click before placing it nearby
bearing.guide.track_observer.text_2: The observer reacts to every train that rolls over its marker
bearing.guide.track_observer.text_3: A filter limits the observer to trains carrying matching cargo
bearing.guide.chain_conveyor.text_1: Holding chains, right-click one conveyor and then another to string them together
bearing.guide.chain_conveyor.text_2: Linked chain conveyors pass rotation on to one another..
bearing.guide.chain_conveyor.text_3: ..and they also hook up to shafts directly above or below
bearing.guide.chain_conveyor.text_4: Right-click a chain with a wrench in hand to ride along it
bearing.guide.chain_conveyor.text_5: Where several chains meet, look at the one you want to take next
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_1: Click a chain conveyor with the frogport, then put it down nearby
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_3: Give it an address in its inventory screen
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_4: Whenever an inserted package carries an address it does not match..
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_6: ..the frogport hands it over to the chain conveyor
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_7: A package with nowhere to go just keeps spinning on the spot
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_8: You can attach as many extra frogports along the chains as you like
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_10: Each package travels the network until it reaches the frog with its address
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_11: A frogport moves items straight into the inventory underneath it
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_12: Packagers work with it too: items get boxed up and sent off in a single step
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_13: A clipboard used on a frogport records the frogport's address
bearing.guide.package_frogport.text_14: Addresses noted on a clipboard are suggested when typing addresses in other screens
bearing.guide.postbox.header: Moving Packages by Train via Postboxes
bearing.guide.postbox.text_1: Click a train station with the postbox, then set it down nearby
bearing.guide.postbox.text_3: Give it an address in its inventory screen
bearing.guide.postbox.text_4: When a package placed inside is meant for another address..
bearing.guide.postbox.text_6: ..and the next train to stop at the station takes it aboard as cargo
bearing.guide.postbox.text_7: In turn, packages carrying this postbox's address are unloaded into it
bearing.guide.postbox.text_9: Packages delivered by train can be pulled out of the postbox
bearing.guide.postbox.text_10: Postboxes, like trains, keep doing their job in unloaded chunks
bearing.guide.postbox.text_11: Packages are still picked up from and dropped into their inventory
bearing.guide.packager.text_1: A packager goes right next to the container whose items it handles
bearing.guide.packager.text_2: Power it with redstone and it gathers the container's items into one package
bearing.guide.packager.text_3: As items, packages are carried and moved like anything else
bearing.guide.packager.text_4: A package put into the packager is opened, and its contents go into the inventory
bearing.guide.packager.text_6: Packagers refuse any package they could not unpack completely
bearing.guide.packager_address.text_2: Put a sign on the packager..
bearing.guide.packager_address.text_4: ..every package it makes carries the sign's text as its address
bearing.guide.packager_address.text_5: Placed in a filter slot, a package filter picks out packages by address
bearing.guide.packager_address.text_10: A mechanical saw opens packages and drops their contents straight on a belt, saving room
bearing.guide.packager_address.text_11: Besides filters, frogports and postboxes can also route packages
bearing.guide.packager_address.text_12: Look them up to learn more about how they behave
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_1: Each newly placed Stock Link begins its own stock network
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_2: To join an existing network, right-click one of its links with the new one, then place it
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_3: Packagers with a link share the contents of their inventory with the network
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_4: Anything on the network can now look up and request what they hold
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_5: When something is requested, the items are packed up from those inventories
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_6: Link signals reach any distance, but the packages still need a way to travel
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_7: At signal strength 15, a link goes silent
bearing.guide.stock_link.text_8: Weaker signals lower its priority, so other links get to act first
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.header: Placing Orders at a Stock Ticker
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_1: Before placing it, right-click a Stock Link to join its network
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_2: Linked packagers offer the items in their inventory to the network
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_3: From a stock ticker, items can be ordered out of those inventories
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_4: Its Stock Keeper is whatever mob or blaze burner sits on a seat facing it
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_5: Orders are placed by right-clicking that keeper
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_6: A submitted order is boxed up into packages
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_7: From there they still have to be brought to where they were ordered
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_8: Attribute or list filters can sort the listed items into categories
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_9: Categories are edited by right-clicking the stock ticker block
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_10: A schematicannon's material list can be ordered here as well
bearing.guide.stock_ticker.text_11: Just give the clipboard printed by the cannon to the Stock Keeper
bearing.guide.stock_ticker_address.text_: An order can be given a destination address when it is placed
Every package made for that order is labelled with this address
Package filters then decide where each of those packages ends up
Besides filters, frogports and postboxes can also route packages
Look them up to learn more about how they behave
bearing.guide.redstone_requester.text_1: Before placing it, right-click a Stock Link to join its network
bearing.guide.redstone_requester.text_2: A redstone requester orders from the network just as a stock ticker does
bearing.guide.redstone_requester.text_3: Its order is configured after a right-click on the requester
bearing.guide.redstone_requester.text_4: Each redstone pulse sends out the order configured there
bearing.guide.redstone_requester.text_5: You can also set a requester up completely before placing it
bearing.guide.redstone_requester.text_6: Use it on a Stock Keeper and choose the order from that menu
bearing.guide.repackager.text_1: Some requests only work if everything shows up in a single package
bearing.guide.repackager.text_5: If not, packages from other orders may slip in between the pieces
bearing.guide.repackager.text_6: In that case, let the packages run into an inventory first
bearing.guide.repackager.text_7: Put a re-packager on it and give it redstone power
bearing.guide.repackager.text_9: As soon as every piece has come in, they leave together as one new package
bearing.guide.repackager.text_10: Requested items now arrive together, in an order you can rely on
bearing.guide.table_cloth.header: Running a Shop on Table Cloths
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_1: Table cloths make a neat surface for showing off items
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_2: Combined with a logistics network, they can turn into a shop
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_3: A shop needs three things first: storage, a Packager and a Stock Link
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_4: Inside the shop, place a Stock Ticker bound to that link
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_5: Give the shop a keeper: a seated mob or blaze burner
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_6: Stock the shop's inventory with whatever is for sale
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_7: To set up a new offer, use a table cloth on the shopkeeper
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_8: The slot on the cloth's side holds the price you ask for
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_9: Now other players can use the shop
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_10: After paying the shopkeeper, the purchased items are boxed up
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_11: From there, they have to be carried to the front of the shop
bearing.guide.table_cloth.text_12: Whatever customers pay ends up in the stock ticker
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_restocker.te: Before placing it, right-click a Stock Link to join its network
A factory gauge fixed onto a packager tracks what that packager's container holds
Use the item to track on the gauge with a right-click
It now displays how many of them the inventory holds
Using the logistics network, the gauge keeps this inventory supplied
Right-click it once more to open its settings
Choose the address the requested items should be sent to
Hold right-click on the gauge to set the amount it should keep in stock
Every time the chest drops below that amount...
...the network ships more of it, labelled with the chosen address
From there, send the packages on into the gauge's packager
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_recipe.text_: When a gauge is placed anywhere other than on a packager...
...it watches the stock of every inventory linked to the network instead
Use the item to track on the gauge with a right-click
It now displays the total number found across the network
To keep that number up, the gauge ships other items off for processing
First, put down a new factory gauge for each ingredient
New connections are made from the target gauge's settings
For looks, a Wrench on an input panel changes the route of its connection
The screen lists the inputs; set how many outputs each batch produces
Next, set where the ingredients get delivered
To choose how many to keep in stock, keep right-click held on the gauge
As soon as stock in the network dips below that number...
...a new batch of ingredients goes out to the chosen address
The products then have to find their way back into a linked inventory
Connections turn green once the target amount has been reached
Add more gauges to the board to cover further steps of a recipe
Every gauge looks after the stock of its own item on its own
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_crafting.tex: Factory gauges can lay out crafting table recipes for you
Hook up each ingredient just like in the previous scene
When the gauge recognises a valid recipe, an extra button shows up in its screen
With that turned on, packages can be unpacked right into the crafters
The crafters must form a 3x3 grid and be joined together with a Wrench
The target count is set by keeping right-click held on the gauge
Gauges with other recipes may share these crafters as well
Send the results back to a linked inventory to complete the cycle
A Re-packager is a good idea so the incoming packages are not split up
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_links.text_1: Adding a connection from the gauge's screen...
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_links.text_2: ...redstone links and display links can be picked as well
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_links.text_3: While the stock meets or beats the target, the redstone link outputs power
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_links.text_4: A link in receive mode can block the gauge's requests
bearing.guide.factory_gauge_links.text_5: Through a display link, the state of every connected gauge can be shown
